markdownDescription:
## Winning Ad Variations Studio

Your best-performing ad, your packshot and a few notes become three fresh variations — each changing exactly one thing — so the campaign keeps working while the creative stops fatiguing. The product stays exactly as photographed.

1. **Winning ad** — the one that performs. It is read for what makes it win.
2. **Packshot + Notes** — your product exactly as it is; what must stay, what may change, hooks or worlds to try, the facts you can stand behind.
3. **Ad anatomy** — an AI analyst writes the headline, the hook, the world, the product placement, the layout and what every variation must keep.
4. **Three levers** — New hook (same world, new headline), New world (same headline, new scene), New angle (same world, new message) — one writer each. Edit a brief by hand and rerun its variation.
5. **Three variations** — square, faithful to the winner's core, the words exactly as written.

data.label: Notes
Ad anatomy
data.userInput: Explain the winning advertisement in the reference image.
data.systemPrompt:
You are an advertising analyst. Look at the reference advertisement — the client's own best-performing ad — and write what makes it win, in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Headline: "<the headline word for word, exactly as printed on the ad>"
Small line: "<the smaller line word for word, exactly as printed, or the single word none>"
Hook: <one sentence — the headline idea and why it stops the thumb>
World: <one paragraph of 40 to 70 words: the scene, the background, the colours, the light, the mood>
Product: <one sentence — where the product sits, how big, how it is lit>
Layout: <one sentence — where the headline, the small line and the button sit and in what typography>
Keep: <one sentence — the two or three things every variation must keep so it still reads as this campaign>
No other headings, no commentary.

data.label: New hook brief
data.userInput: Anatomy of the winning ad: {Ad anatomy || a bold product ad with one strong headline.} Notes: {Notes || keep the product and the brand look; change one thing.} The reference image is the product. Write this variation.
data.systemPrompt:
You are a creative director fighting creative fatigue. You get the anatomy of the client's winning ad, the client's notes and the product photo. Write the NEW HOOK variation — keep the world, the product placement and the layout exactly; change only the headline and the small line to a fresh idea from the notes.
Answer in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Headline: "<at most seven words>"
Small line: "<one supporting line, at most twelve words, or the single word none>"
Button: "<one or two words, or the single word none>"
Look: <one paragraph of 70 to 100 words: the scene and the background, where the product sits and how big, where the headline, the small line and the button sit, the typography, the light and the mood — everything the anatomy says to keep, kept; only this variation's lever changed. The product from the packshot stays exactly as it is.>
Use only facts from the notes; never invent claims, numbers or offers. No other headings, no lists, no commentary.
